list_4_sector_victim_patterns.candidate_lens_A: The third party is the entry point AND the notification blocker: DGFiP (authorised third party's credentials), CEVA (one processor, ten controllers notifying), MyDr (processor cannot notify ~19 M people, ~12,000 clinics must), Retelit (customers learn from a press right-of-reply), Zabka (service-provider account), ACRO (patching contracted out with no internal owner). In every case the compromised party is not the party that owes the notification.
list_4_sector_victim_patterns.candidate_lens_B: Nobody could scope their own incident: DGFiP's post-intrusion access reviews found no theft and only the criminal's sale listing established 678,000 records had gone; NHSBT cannot say who received the pager broadcasts because the network keeps no receiver log; MyDr cannot say what was taken; Retelit's customers report backup-recovery failure at the site certified for continuity; ACRO did not investigate the alerts that would have surfaced a seven-month intrusion.

cross_cutting_themes: Criminal claims validated for once: Fortra confirmed ExfilSquad's published data is genuine for 13 victims and named the likely access path (Power Pages Anonymous Users role) — the opposite outcome to W31, when a vendor assessed the same group's victim list as more likely fabricated.
Disclosure only under external pressure: Retelit (right-of-reply to IrpiMedia), NHSBT (after the BBC raised it), DGFiP (theft established only after the data was advertised for sale).
Public-sector victims choosing reconstruction over restoration (Stiftung Brandenburgische Gedenkstaetten rebuilding IT from scratch across seven sites).

list_6_research_and_actor_developments.candidate_lens_C: The week's tradecraft attacked the record of what happened, not the ability to detect it in the moment: CrowdStrike showing ESXi shell logs capture the pre-expansion command string; Kaspersky's CoolClient driver stripping the implant's own C2 addresses from the network state Windows reports to user mode; Group-IB's intruder using pam_rootok to spend the intrusion wearing ordinary user identities and tampering with auth logs; Sophos's Interlock case where the operator's Volatility3/WinPmem activity is indistinguishable from a real IR engagement on artefact alone; Gunra editing a VDI portal's authentication files so one fixed OTP value always validates. Distinct from the W31 'environmental keying' lens (which was about analysis capability) and from ordinary defence evasion (which is about the detection, not the trail).
list_6_research_and_actor_developments.candidate_lens_D: Access came from something the platform was designed to permit: Jewelbug's native-messaging host named after Edge, the Belgian eID bridge that never checked the caller's origin, ExfilSquad's Power Pages Anonymous Users role, the Trivy scanner LiteLLM's own CI pulled unpinned, coding-agent CI harnesses' allowlists and shared checkouts, Evooo1Bot's enterprise service-account SSH dictionary.
